sentences.text: ORAL ORDER

Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 4.12.2012 passed by the learned Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Main), Narmada at Rajpipla in MAC Petition No. 102 of 2011, the appellant - insurance company has filed this appeal by seriously disputing that deceased as a fare paying passenger travelling in the private car and the operative paragraph 3 whereby the penal interest has been imposed in case the award is not satisfied within 30 days of its pronouncement.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned advocate for the appellant has mainly submitted that tribunal has seriously erred in discarding such contention which was raised in the written statement.
He would further submit that claimant failed to establish the relationship of the deceased with the owner of the vehicle.

In sequel,
it is automatically proved that deceased was gratuitous passenger or fare paying passenger in the errant vehicle and thus there is a clear breach of terms and conditions of the policy and therefore insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: By making above submissions, he would submit to quash the paragraph 3 of the operative order and further to exonerate the insurance company from liability to pay the compensation.
3. Per contra, learned advocate Mr.Hakim would fairly submit that insofar as paragraph 3 of the operative order is concerned, the same may be quashed and set aside.

However, he would submit that in a claim petition, the insurance company has failed to prove any contrast of terms and conditions of the policy as there was no evidence to believe that deceased was gratuitous passenger or she was a passenger for hire and reward.
He would further submit that insurance company has not lead any evidence in this regard and learned tribunal has vividly discussed this issue.
He would therefore submit to dismiss this appeal on the aspect of exonerating the insurance company.

4. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and examined the R & P,
the first submissions of learned advocate for the appellant failed to gain confidence.

Though the insurance company raised the contention that deceased was travelling as gratuitous passenger in the offending vehicle and such vehicle being private car, used for hire and reward can be said to be fundamental breach of the terms and conditions of the policy.
No such evidence to that effect has been led by the insurance company.
The policy being comprehensive package policy and in view of that insurance company has rightly been held liable to pay the compensation.
Therefore this Court does not find NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/713/2013 ORDER DATED: 06/02/2025 undefined any substance in the said submission; accordingly, the same is rejected.

5. Insofar as the direction issued by the tribunal to pay the penal interest @ 9% if the insurance company is failed to deposit the awarded amount within a period of 30 days of announcing the judgment and award is concerned, the same would not sustain as the learned tribunal has no jurisdiction to impose any penal interest while granting interest at 7.5% on the awarded amount.

If the insurance company has failed to follow the mandate of Section 168(3) of the MV Act, the claimant would be entitled to recover the said amount by execution of the impugned the judgment and award.

Section 168(3) of the MV Act does not mandate the tribunal to pass any order of awarding penal interest, if the award is not satisfied within particular period which exercise of power in the opinion of this Court can be said to be excessive in nature and therefore the said finding deserves to be quashed.
6. For the foregoing reasons, the appeal is partly allowed.
The direction issued in paragraph 3 of the operative order of the impugned judgment and award is quashed and set aside while maintaining the rest of the judgment and award as confirmed.

The Tribunal shall disburse the entire awarded amount lying in the FDR and/or with the Tribunal, with accrued interest thereon, if any, to the claimants, by account payee cheque / NEFT / RTGS, after proper verification and after following due procedure and as per the apportionment fixed by the tribunal.
